decision: Access architecture for the first CRA2 Cloud Run demo
decision_limits: No comparative measurements exist on P1. This manifest cannot support preferred. Suitability is a design assessment, not a deployment security pass.

evidence.claim: Direct IAP covers ingress including run.app and permits individual Google principals via roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor.
External or no-organization invitees require external/custom OAuth configuration. The project-specific configuration has not been inspected.
IAP can also be enabled on a load-balancer backend. Direct backend access must be restricted. IAP cannot be enabled at both layers simultaneously.
Application identity should derive from a verified IAP signed assertion with expected issuer, audience and expiry, not a plain email header.
Identity Platform supports Google sign-in. The application must verify ID tokens; the explicit invite allowlist and full-route enforcement would be application work.
Current app uses proxy client host for abuse identity and bounded local SQLite for team memory/telemetry. Deployment identity and persistence tests are still missing.

flip_conditions: If direct IAP fails allowed/denied-user or streaming acceptance in the selected project, test the load-balancer route before adopting it.
If access changes to unrestricted self-service signup or non-Google identity, revisit Identity Platform.
If a load balancer is required for an independently accepted networking requirement, reassess lb-iap with measured results.

unknowns: Full-route authentication middleware and allowlist implementation

priorities.P1: Allowlisted Google identity and no unauthenticated bypass
priorities.P2: Preserve chat behavior and user isolation
priorities.P3: Limit infrastructure and custom authentication maintenance

release_gate: First deployment is for owner acceptance only. Prospective recipients remain pending; no invitations, messages or access grants until owner testing and explicit approval.
